Direction for questions :

Six businessmen from six different cities of the country were invited by the central government to facilitate them for various philanthropic work they did across sectors. The businessmen were given different suites in one hotel and which were in succession and in the same row. Each of them owns a different number of companies and has donated to a different number of NGOs during the last year. The following information is further known: The businessman in Room No. S2 owns twice as many companies as the number of companies owned by the businessman who donated to 8 NGOs in the last year.
The businessman from Udaipur and the businessman in Room S6 together own 40 companies in total.
The businessman from Ahmedabad owns 8 companies less than the businessman from Delhi but donated to 10 more NGOs in the last year.
Four times the number of companies owned by the businessman in room S4 is lesser than the number of NGOs to which he has donated in the last year.
The businessman in S3 owns 12 companies and donated to 8 NGOs last year.
The businessman in S5 owned 8 companies and donated to 2 NGOs less than those donated to by the businessman from Chandigarh in the last year.
The room number given to the Mumbai businessman is an odd number and the businessman from Goa stays in S6.
The businessman from Mumbai is staying two rooms ahead of the Delhi businessman who is staying two rooms ahead of the Chandigarh businessman.

How many companies are owned by the businessman from Delhi?

Direction for questions :

A couple was confused as to what to name their newborn son. So they went to a numerologist and he suggested the following. (A numerologist considers the numerical value of all the letters as A = 1, B = 2, ..., and Z = 26.)
1. It must be a nine-lettered name starting with 'R'.
2. The letter 'H' must appear in the name twice and there must be at least 3 other letters between them.
3. The letter 'Z' should not appear in the name.
4. Exactly one vowel must be repeated and one-third of the letters in the name must be vowels.
5. The sum of the values of all the vowels in the name must be 23.
6. Except for the third position, all other prime-numbered positions in the name must be occupied by vowels.
7. The sum of the values of the first three letters, middle three letters and last three letters in the name must be 26, 43 and 32 respectively.

Between which of the following letters and the middle letter of the name are there definitely 2 other letters?

E. Dalton ate bacon with sauce and also ate eggs.
F. Murdoch, who did not take sauce, ate half as many eggs as the person who ate twice as many slices of bacon as Murdoch did.
G. Bimmy ate four more slices of bacon than Ignatius, but Ignatius ate four more eggs than Bimmy.

Which of the following statements is true?

properties.html:
Direction for questions :

Five Englishmen met at a restaurant and had breakfast comprising of bacon and eggs. The number of slices of bacon consumed are 2, 8, 10, 12 and 16, while the number of eggs consumed are 0, 2, 4, 8 and 12.
Below are some more facts about who eats what and how much.
A. The number of eggs eaten by Ignatius is three times the number of eggs eaten by the person who ate 8 slices of bacon.
B. Three persons, including the one who ate 8 eggs, ate without sauce.
C. Sandhurst did not take any sauce.
D. The one who ate 2 slices of bacon did not eat any eggs or take sauce. Further, he was not Murdoch.
E. Dalton ate bacon with sauce and also ate eggs.
F. Murdoch, who did not take sauce, ate half as many eggs as the person who ate twice as many slices of bacon as Murdoch did.
G. Bimmy ate four more slices of bacon than Ignatius, but Ignatius ate four more eggs than Bimmy.

Which of the following statements is true?

questionFeedback:
Sorry, that's not correct.
Explanation:

Number of eggs eaten = (0, 2, 4, 8, 12)
Number of slices of bacon eaten = (2, 8, 10, 12, 16) From (A), Ignatius ate 3x eggs, the only possibility, is 3x = 12 for x = 4.
∴ The person who ate 8 slices of bacon ate 4 eggs.  ….(i)
From (g), Bimmy ate 12 - 4 = 8 eggs ... (ii)
From (f), Murdoch ate 'y' eggs and 'z' slices of bacon, then one of the persons would have eaten '2y' eggs and '2z' slices of bacon.
∴ y, 2y ∈ (0, 2, 4, 8, 12)
∴ z, 2z ∈ (2, 8, 10, 12, 16)  
∴ z = 8 and 2z = 16

Direction for questions :

Five Englishmen met at a restaurant and had breakfast comprising of bacon and eggs. The number of slices of bacon consumed are 2, 8, 10, 12 and 16, while the number of eggs consumed are 0, 2, 4, 8 and 12.
Below are some more facts about who eats what and how much.
A. The number of eggs eaten by Ignatius is three times the number of eggs eaten by the person who ate 8 slices of bacon.
B. Three persons, including the one who ate 8 eggs, ate without sauce.
C. Sandhurst did not take any sauce.
D. The one who ate 2 slices of bacon did not eat any eggs or take sauce. Further, he was not Murdoch.
E. Dalton ate bacon with sauce and also ate eggs.
F. Murdoch, who did not take sauce, ate half as many eggs as the person who ate twice as many slices of bacon as Murdoch did.
G. Bimmy ate four more slices of bacon than Ignatius, but Ignatius ate four more eggs than Bimmy.

In total how many eggs and bacon did Bimmy eat?
